It reads as bright silver at phone size, warm rather than cool, with no crisp specular on the rims (the P01 note).

Scale: no hard referent remains. Calibrated at 14.5 px/mm on the 72.5 px = 5 mm stone, the soft referents all read plausible at true scale. Paper tooth: band-pass energy sits at 8-20 px wavelength and is absent on the plain surface above the sheet (grain only, 3-5 px). That is ≈0.55-1.4 mm, a normal cold-press. Wash: ≈800-960 px deep (median ≈830, 6.75 pitches), ≈5.7 cm against the 3 cm asked, which errs toward a daintier read, not a bigger one. Visible sheet height: ≈1262 px (y≈498-1760), ≈8.7 cm, a postcard-size card. Bottom deckle: fine (fringe ≈3-5 px, undulation ±5-8 px, ≈0.2-0.55 mm), and finer relative to the units than listing-5's real handmade paper. None of these is tight enough to catch the ≈+60-80% oversize the ferrule exposed in the full frame. The crop hides that error rather than fixing it; this is the same soft-referent basis on which P02_a2c's crop was accepted.

Physics is fine. It is a flat, straight top-down lay with a soft contact shadow below each unit, tinted by the wash under it. The sheet's deckled bottom edge casts a matching downward shadow. A faint lift shadow sits under the sheet's straight top edge at x≈890-920, y≈497-503 (≈4 grey levels; invisible at phone size). Nothing floats, and there is one piece. No text, marks or logos: the calm zone deviates at most 4 grey levels after a grain blur. There is no clipping beyond pavé sparkle (all channels ≥254 on 0.3% of the strip, 0% of the surface).

Palette is on-brand: frame mean (235,221,207), hue 30°, sat 0.11. The surface above the sheet (top 28%) is a warm off-white, (244,234,226) at sat 0.08, the zone r1 called ivory. Its top-right corner drifts to (237,229,225) at sat 0.05, under the Story's profile bar. The sheet is ivory, from (251,239,223) to (241,226,208). The wash runs mint-aqua (hue 150-167°, sat 0.08-0.13), peach-pink (hue 0-12°, sat 0.18-0.22) and butter yellow (hue 41-44°, sat 0.28-0.30). Where aqua overlaps pink, it mixes to a near-neutral grey-lilac band (sat ≈0.02-0.05, val 0.85-0.89). The band runs diagonally from x≈400-520 at the top of the wash to x≈170-260 at its foot. It is real watercolour behaviour, but it is the one muddy note.

Why 8.5 (Story, full plate). 'Watercolour, set in stone.' reads in one second without the brush: the swatch itself says paint, and the stones echo its three colours. The top 28% is calm warm surface for the top-left headline, more room than P02_a2c had. The strip sits at 56-62% of the height, with units ≈10.7% of the width at 1080. It sits at the bar, not above it, for five reasons. The light is soft and flat, with no hard kicker on the rims. The product is a thin line (6% of the height) in a tall frame. The grey overlap band dulls the wash right of centre. Both cuts need a 1.08x upscale. And the right edge kisses the last yellow stone.

The 4:5 box [0,300,1000,1550] (exactly 4:5) changes nothing on fidelity. It keeps the same x-span, so there is still no clasp, latch or brush, and it also drops the deckle and the lower paper. On craft it trades both ways. The strip grows to 8.5% of the height and sits at 56-65%. The calm surface shrinks to the top 16%, plus ≈10% clean paper above the wash, and the sheet's straight top edge runs through the headline zone at 16% (dark type works on both tones). The bottom edge cuts the wash's ragged lower edge: paper shows below it at x<350, and the wash runs off at x≈650-750. Net: the same 8.5 and the same verdict.
